Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — model fit & tool-calling evals (next steps)

Hi Samir / Emily —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the clear context on the three core success criteria you shared (latency <250ms P95, JSON schema compliance for payment routing, and <2% critical-field regression). Per our conversation, I pulled together a concise plan to run a targeted model-fit evaluation with tool/function calling and structured output checks.

Quick recap + recommendations:
- Recommended model candidates: Redwood-2.7B-quant (fast, cheaper baseline) and Llama-3-13B-rt (higher quality for rarer intents).
- Eval focus: schema-compliant JSON output (payment_routing schema), function-calling reliability (retries, idempotency), and regression detection vs your golden prompts.
- Artifacts attached: redwood_model_fit_proposal.pdf (scope & timeline), prompt_set_v2.jsonl (sample prompts + negative cases).

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a 500-1k sample of anonymized transactions and the canonical JSON schema for routing (we can accept a redacted sample).
2) We run a 1-week model-fit run with both model candidates using our tool-calling harness (includes structured-output validator and automatic retry traces).
3) Checkpoint call after run (we suggest 30-45 minutes) to review results, failure modes, and quantized recommendations.

If that sounds good I can kick off scheduling and loop in our eval engineer (Aditya) and security for the compliance checklist.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan — this aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifying Qs before we share data: 

1) JSON schema validation: how strict is the validator? Do you support partial object validation and clear error categories (missing required field vs type mismatch vs extraneous fields)? We need deterministic failure categories for our downstream automation.

2) Retries & idempotency: in the tool-calling flow, how are retries surfaced in the logs and what guarantees do we get around double-processing? For example, if the model triggers two function calls for the same payment, how do we avoid duplicate charge attempts?

3) PII and data handling: we’ll redact account numbers but will still include tokenized identifiers — what is your recommended redaction approach so the eval is realistic but compliant?

If you can answer these briefly we’ll prepare a redacted sample and the schema. Also Emily and I are available for the checkpoint week of 31 May.

Best,
Samir
Director of Product | FinServe
Samir.Patel@finserve.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — model fit & tool-calling evals (next steps)

Samir — great questions, answered inline below. Looping in Rishi (security) for the PII handling note and Aditya (evals) for test-harness specifics.

1) JSON schema validation:
- We run a layered validation: (a) shallow structural check (required fields + types), (b) detailed semantic checks (enum values, format regex), and (c) post-processing business rules (cross-field consistency).
- Validation results are categorized into: required_missing, type_mismatch, format_violation, extraneous_field, semantic_error. Each failure has a classifier and example failing payload so downstream automation can map to deterministic handlers.

2) Retries & idempotency for function-calling:
- Our harness records each model->function intent and assigns a deterministic call id derived from message hash + prompt id. Retries are logged as replays of the same call id (not new ids) so downstream functions can deduplicate.
- We also provide a configurable client-side retry policy (exponential backoff + max attempts) and an idempotency header you can surface to payment systems.
- In the rare case the model emits multiple distinct function calls for the same logical operation, our post-processor flags duplicates and marks the segment for manual review; we include metrics on duplicate-call rate in the report.

3) PII/data handling:
- Recommended: replace account numbers with stable tokens (acct_tok_<hash>) and keep a separate mapping file stored in your vault. That preserves distributional properties for the eval while removing raw PII.
- Rishi, can you add a short checklist for the redaction/ingestion pipeline?

Attachments: eval_checklist.xlsx

Proposed next steps (concrete):
A) FinServe shares 1k redacted samples + canonical schema link (shared drive).
B) We start a 5-business-day run using the two model candidates and our tool-calling harness. Run will output: per-prompt JSON validation result, function-call traces (with call ids), and a regression delta report vs your golden set.
C) Checkpoint call week of 31 May — we’ll bring the initial run artifacts and a recommended quantization profile.

Samir/Emily — does this plan and timing work? If yes I’ll send a calendar invite and Aditya will kick off the job as soon as we have the sample.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa / Rishi —

Quick internal note to confirm the run details so we can be ready when FinServe sends samples:
- Harness: structured-output-validator v2 (schema categories + example payloads), function-trace-logger v1.4.
- Models: Redwood-2.7B-quant (batch=4, context=1024), Llama-3-13B-rt (batch=2, context=2048).
- Retries: client policy = exp_backoff (0.5s initial, factor=2, max_attempts=3). Call-id generation = sha256(prompt_id + message_hash) trimmed to 16 chars.
- Output artifacts: validation_report.csv, function_traces.jsonl, regression_delta.csv.
- Estimated cost (infra + eval hours): ~$1,200 for 5 business days in us-west-2 on our reserved capacity.

I attached a run_config_stub.yaml (small template) and will update with exact infra ids after we get the sample and confirm region.

I’ll stand up the job the day we receive the data and post the S3 link to the drive folder.
